newsitem.title: USA: Ford CEO sees improved results in Europe, Latam.
newsitem.headline: Ford CEO sees improved results in Europe, Latam.

text.p: Ford Motor Co board chairman and chief executive Alex Trotman said on Wednesday he expected improved results next year from operations in Europe and Latin America.
He told Reuters Ford should see better results as the company got large-scale production underway in those regions.

"With a major launch of high-volume production you are always going to incur unusual costs -- downtime, large expense of installing new equipment, and so forth. Once you're up and running you're through that period and away you go," Trotman said.
He added, "I expect next year to be a better year in Europe (and Latin America)."
Ford lost $472 million in the third quarter in Europe and $226 million in Latin America, mostly in Brazil.
Trotman, who was in New York to receive an award from the United States Council for International Business, declined to offer forecasts of fourth quarter results from those regions.

He also said Ford had no plans to continue an early retirement program for employees. About 4000 workers will take advantage of the program this year and Ford has said it expects to record a charge of $300 to $400 million in the fourth quarter from the plan.
"We haven't made any plans at all for continuation of the package that we talked about. It's not meant to continue," Trotman said.
